decision_reason: A1 separates sitting and standing only through global inclination and separates the two lying postures through smoothness, which is not a necessary physical difference between static postures. Add leg inclination and lateral torso inclination to represent these distinctions directly. Basketball has the weakest supplied seen coverage; add intensity variability to express its intermittent motion using transferable seen anchors. Preserve the other A1 concepts because additional distinctions among exercise-machine activities would require uncertain assumptions about technique. The supplied distances guide these choices but do not establish predictability or recognition performance.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

attributes.name: upper_leg_inclination
attributes.definition: Typical inclination of the upper legs' longitudinal axes relative to vertical within a window, averaged across both legs and independent of torso inclination.

levels.Low: Upper legs remain predominantly near vertical.
levels.Medium: Upper legs are typically oblique or move between near-vertical and near-horizontal orientations.
levels.High: Upper legs remain predominantly near horizontal.

attributes.name: torso_lateral_inclination
attributes.definition: Magnitude of the torso's gravity-relative tilt out of its anatomical sagittal plane, irrespective of left or right direction.

levels.Low: Gravity lies predominantly within the torso's sagittal plane, with little lateral tilt.
levels.Medium: Gravity has a substantial lateral component, indicating oblique lateral tilt.
levels.High: Gravity lies predominantly along the torso's left-right axis, indicating near-sideways torso orientation.

attributes.name: intensity_variability
attributes.definition: Extent of changes in the overall motion-energy envelope within a window, beyond fluctuations within individual repeated movement cycles.

levels.Low: Motion intensity remains approximately steady across the window.
levels.Medium: Motion intensity undergoes moderate changes across the window.
levels.High: Motion intensity changes markedly between quieter and more vigorous intervals.

operations.reason: motion_intensity: G3 supports overall acceleration and rotation magnitude, retaining a broad contrast between static activities and vigorous running or basketball. Jumping and the cross trainer provide vigorous seen anchors. Effort, technique and window content can alter magnitude; intensity alone cannot identify an activity.

operations.reason: cadence: G6 supports repetition rate in repeated leg and body motion, transferring from walking and cycling to running and upright cycling. Harmonics, different meaningful cycle units and freely chosen cycling pace create ambiguity; the activity names do not guarantee a particular cadence.

operations.reason: smoothness: G9 supports sustained rapid changes in acceleration and rotation, preserving transfer between continuous machine exercise and fluctuating locomotor or sports motion. Technique and movement intensity affect this evidence. Static supine and side lying have no necessary smoothness difference, so their A1 distinction should not be treated as physically required.

operations.reason: impulsiveness: G10 supports brief abrupt changes associated with foot contacts or landings, providing transfer from jumping and stair descent to running and basketball. Contact style, sensor attachment and windows without landings can weaken or alter the evidence.

contrast_unseen: cycling on an exercise bike in vertical positions

operations.reason: posture_inclination: G1 supports mean gravity-relative body orientation, retaining upright-to-recumbent transfer from standing in an elevator and supine lying. Sitting is a mixed torso-leg configuration, so its global inclination is less unambiguous than recumbency; dynamic acceleration also complicates posture estimation.

posture_variability: G12 supports changing gravity-relative global posture. Rowing and moving around in an elevator provide seen examples of posture change relevant to basketball. Limb swings alone do not establish global posture variation, and short basketball windows may contain little postural change.

rotational_motion: G2 supports angular motion in the torso and limbs, transferring repeated leg rotation from horizontal cycling to vertical cycling and vigorous angular motion to running. Pedaling, limb swings and body turns can produce similar overall rotational prominence, limiting activity specificity.

operations.reason: translational_motion: G13 supports short-window translational-motion proxies, preserving a distinction between locomotor activity and stationary exercise. Parking-lot walking offers a locomotor anchor for basketball. Sustained velocity is weakly observable from IMUs, and treadmill progression, elevator travel and local body oscillation can be ambiguous; retain this as a coarse semantic concept without asserting reliable absolute translation.

operations.reason: motion_regularity: G6 and G11 support recurrence and temporal predictability, connecting steady treadmill exercise to running and less predictable elevator movement to basketball. A static posture can be highly regular without periodic motion; short sports segments can also appear regular.

operations.reason: upper_leg_inclination: G1 supports gravity-relative orientation from the leg IMUs. Predominantly horizontal upper legs in ordinary sitting versus predominantly vertical upper legs in standing provide a second physical contrast beyond global posture. Supine lying and standing in an elevator provide seen orientation endpoints. Interpretation requires consistent anatomical sensor alignment; leg placement, seating style and dynamic acceleration introduce ambiguity, so cycling variants should not be assigned different levels merely from their names.

torso_lateral_inclination: G1 supports the direction of gravity relative to the torso, and G14 supports the associated multiaxial structure. Side lying places gravity largely along the torso's left-right axis, unlike supine lying, providing an independent physical distinction without relying on smoothness. Seen supine and upright postures anchor the low state, but no supplied seen class guarantees sustained high lateral inclination; high-state zero-shot prediction therefore has limited seen support. Anatomical alignment and oblique rolling are additional ambiguities.

intensity_variability: G4 supports changes in motion magnitude over time. Alternation between quieter movement and vigorous actions provides a plausible transferable description of basketball's weakly covered semantics; moving around in an elevator supplies variable motion while steady treadmill walking supplies a more constant anchor. This concerns the energy envelope rather than impact peaks or recurrence. Basketball may remain vigorous throughout a short window, and repeated gait or rowing cycles must not automatically imply high variability; predictability depends on window duration and activity phase.

cycling on an exercise bike in vertical positions
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)

semantic_redundancy_review: All nine A1 attributes are retained exactly, and three additions supply separate physical concepts. Upper-leg inclination describes segment posture rather than global inclination; lateral torso inclination describes the direction of recumbency rather than its overall magnitude. Intensity variability describes changes in the motion-energy envelope, whereas intensity describes its magnitude, smoothness sustained rapid change, impulsiveness brief peaks, cadence repetition rate, and regularity predictability. Posture variability concerns configuration changes, not arbitrary angular motion. No extra arm-use, flight-phase or pedaling-geometry attributes are introduced because the supplied semantics do not establish stable additional distinctions. Stepper versus cross trainer and the two cycling configurations remain partly dependent on existing A1 concepts; no unsupported differences are manufactured. This refinement defines an ontology only and does not validate A1 prototype assignments or claim improved distances or accuracy.
